mainTopic: מעשר בהמה: the doubtful ראש השנה case, the tithing procedure, and what is required for the tenth to become holy
overview: This amud opens at the end of רבא's case about animals born in אב, אלול, and תשרי, when we are unsure whether the ראש השנה for מעשר בהמה is א' אלול or א' תשרי. With a ממה נפשך, רבא rules that one animal is taken from the אלול group and the rest are exempt. The leftovers do not join a later גורן, because the Torah requires a definite tenth (עשירי ודאי), not a ספק. A new משנה then describes the tithing procedure: the animals pass one at a time through a narrow opening, are counted, and the tenth is painted red and declared מעשר. Skipping the paint, the rod, or the walking out does not cancel the tithe after the fact. Taking a tenth without counting is a מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The משנה also covers a counted animal, or the holy tenth, jumping back into the pen. The גמרא brings a ברייתא: the mothers stand outside and call the young out, since 'יעבור' means the animal must pass on its own, and רב הונא explains why the mothers are used rather than food. A second ברייתא derives from the פסוק the exclusion of a טריפה and the rules for imperfect counting and for not naming the animal 'tenth'. The amud ends by explaining רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view through אבא אלעזר בן גומל's comparison of תרומה גדולה and תרומת מעשר, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא rules: take one animal from the אלול group
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that one animal is taken as מעשר from the animals born in אלול, and all the others are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he takes one of the אלול-born animals as tithe, and the rest are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining רבא's ruling at its end. His case is five animals born in אב, five in אלול, and five in תשרי, when we do not know which date starts the year for מעשר בהמה. He rules that only one animal is taken, from the אלול group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals only combine toward a count of ten if they belong to the same tithe year. Since the new year date is in doubt, רבא looks for the one group that is definitely part of a full group of ten. That group is אלול.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe of animals: every tenth animal is sanctified
Animals born in the month of אלול

phrases.english: and he takes one of the Elul-born animals
phrases.notes: This continues רבא's statement on the previous amud.

phrases.english: and the remainder are exempt,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's ruling, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the doubt between א' אלול and א' תשרי, take one tithe animal from the אלול group; the rest are exempt.

steps.title: Why אלול works under either opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains with a ממה נפשך argument: whichever date is ראש השנה, the אלול animals are part of a group of ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if the new year is on the first of אלול, then אלול and תשרי combine and the אב animals are exempt. If the new year is on the first of תשרי, then אב and אלול combine and the תשרי animals are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason for his ruling by checking both possible dates for ראש השנה. Under each one, the אלול animals end up in a combined group of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the year starts in אלול, the אלול and תשרי animals share a year, while the אב animals belong to the old year. If the year starts in תשרי, the אב and אלול animals share a year, while the תשרי animals belong to the new year. Either way exactly one group of ten exists, and it always includes אלול, so one tithe from אלול is certainly correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you take it: an argument that works under both possibilities
The start of the year for counting animal tithe
Combine together toward the count of ten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is about the regular ראש השנה in תשרי. Here it means the new year for מעשר בהמה, which רבי מאיר places on א' אלול and others on א' תשרי.

phrases.english: whichever way you look at it:
if the new year is on the first of Elul —
those of Elul and Tishrei combine
and those of Av are exempt,
and if the new year is on the first of Tishrei —
those of Av and Elul combine
those of Tishrei are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under both possible new-year dates, the אלול animals are in a group of ten, so taking from אלול is always valid.

steps.title: Why not combine the leftovers with a later group?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the leftover animals should not simply be exempt. Let them join with animals of another גורן (tithing round).
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you say? Let them combine with another gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge against calling the leftover animals "exempt." Why not save them and count them together with animals at a later tithing round?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals not yet tithed usually wait and join the next round of tithing. So it seems wrong to free the leftover אב or תשרי animals completely when they could be counted later.

keyTerms.meaning: What would you say? (introduces a possible objection)
A gathering of animals for tithing (literally "threshing floor")

phrases.english: What would you say:
let them combine with another gathering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the "rest are exempt" part of רבא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the leftover animals are fully exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Untithed animals normally wait for a later round, so the leftovers should join the next גורן instead of being exempt.

steps.title: The Torah requires a definite tenth
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the Torah demands a definite tenth (עשירי ודאי), not a doubtful one. The leftover animals are each in ספק, so they cannot be counted toward a tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One said a definite tenth, and not an uncertain one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Animals of doubtful status cannot be counted, because the Torah requires the tenth animal to be definitely the tenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any leftover animal may have already belonged to a counted group of ten, depending on which date is ראש השנה. If such animals joined a later group, the animal marked as "tenth" would only be a doubtful tenth. The פסוק "הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ" requires a certain tenth, so the doubtful animals are simply exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: מעשר בהמה only applies to a definite tenth (עשירי ודאי). Animals whose count status is in ספק are exempt, and they do not join a later group.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle עשירי ודאי ולא ספק is a key rule of מעשר בהמה. It explains why doubt leads to exemption here rather than to stringency.

phrases.english: the Merciful One said a definite tenth,
and not an uncertain one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leftovers should be counted with a later round.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doubtful animals cannot produce a definite tenth, so they are exempt.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say to take one from the אלול animals. Isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רבא's ruling needed to be stated at all. It is setting up the next step, which will explain what רבא is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under both views the אלול animals are surely part of a group of ten. So it seems needless to say that a tithe is taken from them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (challenges the need to state something)

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the leftovers back to the need for רבא's main ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבא to state that one takes from the אלול animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The certainty of the אלול group is self-evident, so stating it adds nothing.

steps.title: No rabbinic decree against tithing the אלול animals
steps.stepSummary: Answer: we might have thought the חכמים would make a גזירה against tithing even the אלול animals, out of fear one would take from the others. רבא teaches that there is no such decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said we should decree against it, lest he come to take from those others. It teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point in רבא's ruling. Someone might think the חכמים would forbid tithing at all here, out of worry about mistakes. רבא teaches that they did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the owner might mix up the groups and take a tithe from the doubtful אב or תשרי animals. רבא's ruling shows we do not make that גזירה, and one does tithe from the אלול animals.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

phrases.english: you might have said we should decree,
lest he come to take from those others,
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן: the ruling rejects a possible גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים might forbid tithing from the אלול animals, fearing mix-ups with the doubtful groups.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such גזירה is made; one tithes from the אלול animals.

steps.title: New משנה: how is tithing done?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens by asking how animals are tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In what manner does one tithe?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a question about the practical method of tithing animals. It is setting up the description that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was which animals join together. Now the משנה shifts to the actual procedure of separating מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
In what manner does one tithe?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on the tithing procedure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical procedure for separating מעשר בהמה

steps.title: The tithing procedure
steps.stepSummary: The animals are gathered in a pen and leave through a narrow opening one at a time. They are counted, and the tenth is marked with red paint and declared מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He gathers them into a pen and makes a small opening for them, so that two cannot go out together. He counts: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. The one that goes out tenth he marks with red paint and says: "This is tithe."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the ideal way to tithe. The animals walk out one by one, and the tenth is marked and declared holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The narrow opening makes sure each animal is counted on its own, so the tenth is exact. The red paint (סיקרא) marks the tithe animal so it is not mixed up with the others, and the declaration names it as מעשר.

phrases.english: he gathers them into a pen,
and makes a small opening for them
so that two will not
be able to go out together,
and they count: one, two, three, four,
five, six, seven, eight, nine,
and the one that goes out tenth he marks with red paint
and says: "This is tithe."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the משנה's opening question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animals leave one by one through a narrow opening, are counted, and the tenth is painted red and declared מעשר.

steps.title: Skipped details do not cancel the tithe
steps.stepSummary: After the fact, the tithe still takes effect if he did not paint the animal, did not count with a rod, or counted the animals lying or standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not mark it with red paint, or did not count them with the rod, or counted them while lying down or standing, these are still tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that the ideal procedure is not required after the fact (בדיעבד). The tithe still works even if steps were skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The painting, the counting with a rod (שבט), and the walking out are the proper way to tithe. They are not conditions without which the tithe fails. What matters is that a tenth animal was counted and designated.

keyTerms.meaning: Rod or staff used in counting (from the פסוק "תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט")

steps.whatToRemember: The procedure of the narrow opening, counting with the rod, and red paint is the ideal method (לכתחילה). Skipping it does not cancel the tithe after the fact (בדיעבד).
steps.confusionAlert: Even though the פסוק mentions passing "under the rod," counting without a rod still works after the fact. The rod is the proper method, not a requirement for validity.

phrases.english: if he did not mark it with red paint,
or did not count them with the rod,
or counted them lying down or standing —
these are tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the procedure of step 8 to the ideal method, not a requirement for validity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tithing works after the fact even without the red paint, the rod, or the walking out through the opening.

steps.title: Taking a tenth without counting
steps.stepSummary: If someone takes ten out of one hundred, or one out of ten, without counting them one by one, the תנא קמא says it is not מעשר. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had one hundred animals and took ten, or had ten and took one, that is not tithe. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it is tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its rules for tithing. It now rules on an owner who simply picks out a tenth without doing the counting at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said that skipping details like the paint or the rod does not ruin the tithe after the fact. Here the counting itself was skipped, so the תנא קמא says the animal is not holy at all. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that the right amount alone is enough, even without counting.

keyTerms.meaning: this is not tithe; it does not become holy

phrases.english: If he had one hundred and took ten,
or ten and took one —
phrases.notes: He simply picked them out without counting.

phrases.english: that is not tithe.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says: it is tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 9: missing details are allowed after the fact, but missing the counting itself is a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a tenth taken without counting is not מעשר. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that it is.

steps.title: An animal jumps back into the pen
steps.stepSummary: If a counted animal jumps back among the uncounted ones, they are all exempt. If the designated tenth jumps back, all of them must graze until they get a blemish and are then eaten by the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the counted animals jumped back among them, they are all exempt. If one of the tithed animals jumped back among them, they must all graze until they become blemished, and then they are eaten in their blemished state by the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a mix-up during counting, when an animal that already went out jumps back into the pen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an ordinary counted animal jumps back, each animal in the pen might be that one, which cannot be counted again. So none of them can be tithed and they are exempt. If the holy tenth jumps back, any animal might be holy. So none may be used as ordinary food until it gets a blemish, and then the owner may eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: animals already counted (ordinary, not the tenth)
animals designated as the holy tenth
they graze until they become unfit (blemished)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. 'מנויין' are ordinary counted animals, so the pen becomes exempt. 'מעושרין' are the holy tenth, so every animal in the pen becomes doubtful and must wait for a blemish.
steps.whatToRemember: A counted animal mixing back in makes the rest exempt. A holy tenth mixing back in means all of them graze until they are blemished.

phrases.english: If one of the counted ones jumped back among them —
these are exempt,
phrases.notes: Any of them might be the one already counted.

phrases.english: if one of the tithed ones jumped back among them —
all of them graze until they become blemished,
and they are eaten in their blemished state by the owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the case of a mix-up during the counting process.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A counted animal mixing back in exempts the pen. A designated tenth mixing back in requires all of them to graze until they are blemished, after which the owner eats them.

steps.title: The ברייתא describes the tithing procedure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. The animals are gathered in a pen with a narrow opening, the mothers stand outside and bleat, and the young animals come out one at a time toward them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: In what way does one tithe? He gathers them into a pen and makes a small opening for them, so that two cannot go out together. Their mothers are outside and they are inside. The mothers bleat, and the young ones go out toward their mothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that gives more detail about how the animals leave the pen. This sets up the next questions about why it is done this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said that the animals leave through a narrow opening. The ברייתא adds the method: the mothers outside call, so the young come out on their own. The next steps of the גמרא challenge this specific method.

phrases.english: GEMARA. The Rabbis taught:
In what way does one tithe?
He gathers them into a pen,
and makes a small opening for them

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ שְׁנַיִם יְכוֹלִין לָצֵאת כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: so that two will not be able to go out together,
their mothers are outside and they are inside,
and the mothers bleat, and the young go out toward their mothers.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה/תשובה (the ברייתא asks and answers its own question)
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּאֵי זֶה צַד מְעַשֵּׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's description from step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The young animals exit through a narrow opening, one by one, drawn out by their bleating mothers.

steps.title: Why not just push them out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the owner does not simply drive the animals out himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him take them out himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's method. Why go to the trouble of using the mothers when the owner could just push the animals out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the mothers seems unnecessary. Pushing the animals through the narrow opening would also bring them out one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: but let him take them out

phrases.english: But let him take them out himself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method described in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's requirement to use the mothers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler method, pushing the animals out, would seem to work just as well.

steps.title: The פסוק requires the animal to pass on its own
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'יעבור', meaning 'it passes'. The animal must go out by itself, not be made to pass.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'passes', and not that they make it pass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah's wording requires the animal to walk out on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'כל אשר יעבור תחת השבט' uses the simple form 'יעבור', meaning it passes by itself. Pushing would be 'making it pass', which the פסוק excludes. So the animal needs a reason to walk out on its own.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why there must be an outside draw at all. The only remaining question is what that draw should be.

phrases.english: 'It passes' is written,
and not that they make it pass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Derivation from the wording of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner could simply push the animals out.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יעבור' requires the animal to pass on its own, so it cannot be pushed.

steps.title: Why not lure them out with food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the owner does not throw vegetables outside so the animals come out to eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him throw them a vegetable, and they will go out toward it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the animals must come out on their own. It now asks why the mothers are needed, since food would also draw them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food would also make the animals walk out by themselves, which satisfies 'יעבור'. So the mothers still seem unnecessary.

phrases.english: But let him throw them a vegetable
and they will go out toward it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge that builds on the answer of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to use the mothers specifically
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food also makes the animals pass on their own, so it should meet the 'יעבור' requirement just as well.

steps.title: רב הונא: a גזירה because of purchased and orphaned animals
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says using the mothers is a rabbinic decree. It keeps purchased and orphaned animals, which are exempt from tithe, from coming out and being counted by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is a decree because of a purchased animal and because of an orphan.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains why the חכמים required the mothers rather than food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A purchased animal and an orphan are exempt from מעשר. Food would draw them out together with the others, and they might be counted by mistake. A purchased animal's mother is not in the flock, and an orphan has no mother, so no one calls them and they stay inside.

keyTerms.meaning: an orphan animal whose mother died before it was born (exempt)

steps.whatToRemember: The animals must leave the pen on their own because of 'יעבור'. The חכמים required the mothers to be the draw, rather than food, so that exempt animals stay behind.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is a decree because of a purchased animal and because of an orphan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם לָקוּחַ וּמִשּׁוּם יָתוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Food would work just as well as the mothers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים required the mothers so that exempt purchased and orphaned animals would not come out and be counted.

steps.title: A טריפה is excluded from animal tithe
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'כל אשר יעבור תחת השבט' to exclude a טריפה, since it cannot pass under the rod.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Whatever passes under the rod.' This excludes a טריפה, which does not pass under the rod.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that learns rules of מעשר בהמה from the words of the פסוק. Its first rule is that a טריפה is not part of the tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes animals that 'pass under the rod.' A טריפה is an animal with a fatal defect, and the ברייתא treats it as something that cannot properly 'pass' under the rod. So it is left out of מעשר בהמה altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect
The rod used to count and mark the animals

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Whatever passes under" (the rod)
excluding a tereifa,
which does not pass under the rod.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of how the animals leave the pen, a new ברייתא learns more laws from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טריפה is excluded from מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: The proper way is to count with a rod
steps.stepSummary: The ideal way to count the animals is with a rod.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a מצוה to count them with a rod.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states the proper method of counting: with a שבט. This sets up the next question, which asks what happens if the counting was not done this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'תחת השבט' are read as instructions for how to count. The ברייתא calls this a מצוה, which is the ideal way. The next step asks whether it is required for the tithe to take effect, and step 20 answers that it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: The proper, ideal way to perform the act

phrases.english: It is a מצוה to count them with a rod.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same phrase 'תחת השבט.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Counting with a שבט is the ideal way (a מצוה).

steps.title: What if the counting was not done properly?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the tenth is holy even if it was not counted with a rod, or was counted lying down or standing still.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not count them with a rod, or he counted them while they were lying down or standing, from where do we know that the tenth is still holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks about cases where the counting was not done the ideal way. Does the tenth animal still become holy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the animals walk past one at a time under the rod. Here they were counted without a rod, or while lying or standing in place. The ברייתא looks for a source that the tithe still takes effect.

phrases.english: If he did not count them with a rod,
or he counted them lying down or standing,
from where (do we know the tenth is holy)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the מצוה from Step 18 is required for the tithe to take effect.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the tenth is holy even when the counting was not done the ideal way.

steps.title: 'The tenth shall be holy' — in any case
steps.stepSummary: The words 'העשירי יהיה קודש' teach that the tenth is holy no matter how the counting was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The tenth shall be holy' — in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the words 'העשירי קודש.' The tenth animal is holy even without the rod and even if the animals were not walking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses the result: whatever is tenth is holy. So the rod and the walking are the ideal way, but they are not needed for the tithe to take effect.

phrases.english: The verse states: "The tenth shall be holy"
in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tenth is holy even if it was not counted with a rod or while walking.
steps.whyThisMatters: It separates the ideal way (counting with a rod) from what is needed for the tithe to take effect (the animal being tenth).

steps.title: What if he never called it 'tenth'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the animal is holy even if the owner never said 'this is the tenth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this when he called it 'tenth.' If he did not call it 'tenth,' from where do we know it is holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another weakness in the process: the owner counted correctly but never named the animal 'tenth.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we knew the tenth is holy when it was actually named 'tenth.' Now the ברייתא asks whether naming it is required.

phrases.english: I only know this when he called it "tenth";
if he did not call it "tenth," from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁקְּרָא שְׁמוֹ עֲשִׂירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 20 and pushes the leniency one step further.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the tenth is holy even without being named 'tenth.'

steps.title: 'Shall be holy' — even without naming it
steps.stepSummary: The words 'יהיה קודש' teach that the tenth is holy even if it was never called 'tenth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Shall be holy' — in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the word 'יהיה' (shall be). The tenth becomes holy on its own, even without being named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Shall be holy' means it automatically becomes holy. Saying the word 'tenth' is not needed. The counting is what matters.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Shall be holy"
in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Naming the animal 'tenth' is not required; the tenth becomes holy automatically.

steps.title: What if he just took a tenth without counting?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that someone who took ten out of a hundred, or one out of ten, without counting might have tithed his animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: if he had a hundred and took ten, or had ten and took one, perhaps they should count as tithed?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now checks the limit of all this leniency. What if there was no counting at all, and he simply grabbed a tenth of the animals?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps so far showed that the method of counting and the naming do not matter. Following that trend, one might think the counting itself is not needed either, as long as the amount taken is a tenth.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל הָיוּ לוֹ מֵאָה וְנָטַל עֲשָׂרָה,
phrases.english: One might think: if he had a hundred and took ten,
or ten and took one,
one might think they should be tithed?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל הָיוּ לוֹ מֵאָה וְנָטַל עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the 'מכל מקום' leniencies of Steps 20 and 22 reach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether taking a tenth without any counting counts as tithing.

steps.title: Without counting, it is not 'the tenth'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'עשירי' teaches that an animal taken without counting is not 'the tenth,' so it is not tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'tenth,' and this one is not the tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says no. The animal must actually be the tenth in a count, so taking one without counting does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the limit. Counting the wrong way or not naming the animal is acceptable, but there must be real counting. An animal that was just taken was never 'tenth' at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is not the tenth

steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא קמא, the counting can be imperfect and the animal does not need to be named, but there must be an actual count that makes this animal the tenth.

phrases.english: The verse states: "tenth,"
and this is not the tenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עֲשִׂירִי וְאֵין זֶה עֲשִׂירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 by rejecting the suggestion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without counting, the animal is not tithe.

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה: it is tithe
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagrees and holds that an animal taken without counting is tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it is tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא argues with the last ruling. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that taking one out of ten, even without counting, makes it מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, removing the correct amount is enough, and a formal count is not required. This disagreement is what the גמרא now sets out to explain.
steps.confusionAlert: The one word 'מעשר' is his full ruling: 'it IS tithe.' He is not starting a new topic.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says: It is tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling of Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking a tenth without counting still makes it tithe.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now speaks in its own voice and asks why רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rules this way, since the פסוק seems to say 'tenth.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא had a clear source in the word 'עשירי.' The גמרא wants to know what lets רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה accept a tithe without a count.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion in Step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: He follows אבא אלעזר בן גומל's comparison of the two תרומות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה follows אבא אלעזר בן גומל, who reads the פסוק as comparing תרומה גדולה and תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He agrees with אבא אלעזר בן גומל. As a ברייתא teaches: אבא אלעזר בן גומל says, 'And your תרומה shall be reckoned to you' — the פסוק is talking about two תרומות: one is תרומה גדולה and the other is תרומת מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה follows אבא אלעזר בן גומל and quotes his ברייתא. That ברייתא says one פסוק puts two kinds of תרומה side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תרומתכם' (your תרומה) is read as covering two תרומות, which puts them in the same category. Because the two are linked, rules that apply to one can be carried over to the other. The next step will show which rule is carried over.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose teaching is quoted here
The main תרומה given to the כהן from the crop
The tenth the לוי gives to the כהן from his own tithe

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up תרומת מעשר (a produce gift from the לוי to the כהן) with מעשר בהמה (animal tithe). The link back to animals is only about the method of separating.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּאַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גּוֹמֵל,
phrases.english: He holds like Abba Elazar ben Gomel,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גּוֹמֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Abba Elazar ben Gomel says:
"And your teruma shall be reckoned to you"
the verse speaks of two terumot:
one is standard teruma,
and one is teruma of the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּאַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גּוֹמֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26 by naming the source behind רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He follows אבא אלעזר בן גומל, who links תרומה גדולה and תרומת מעשר.

steps.title: תרומה גדולה can be taken by estimate and by thought
steps.stepSummary: אבא אלעזר בן גומל begins the comparison: תרומה גדולה may be taken by estimate and by thought alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as תרומה גדולה is taken by estimate and by thought...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup for the comparison. It states the rule for תרומה גדולה, and the next lines (on the next amud) will apply the same rule to תרומת מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה גדולה has no fixed measured amount, so it can be taken by estimate. It can even be set aside by thought, without physically separating it. This 'just as...' line is the first half of the comparison, and it will lead back to explaining why a tenth taken without counting can still work.

phrases.english: Just as standard teruma
is taken by estimate and by thought —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַתְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה נִיטֶּלֶת בְּאוֹמֶד וּבְמַחְשָׁבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins spelling out what follows from linking the two תרומות in Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומה גדולה may be separated by estimate and by thought (the first half of the comparison).
